excerpt_original: Read a selection of the individual ballots submitted by our voters for the Best Films of 2025 category

blocks.text: The results are in for our 2025 poll of Film Comment ’s contributors and colleagues! On this page you’ll find a selection of the individual ballots submitted by our voters for the Best Films of 2025 category, covering features that were released either theatrically or virtually in 2025 in the United States. To see which films came out on top, check out our Best Films of 2025 list, which features original appreciations from critics, as well as links to features, reviews, and interviews about these films and directors from across the year.

Don’t see your favorite? Check out our Best Undistributed Films of 2025 list, featuring films that premiered this year but have not yet announced stateside distribution. And don’t miss our Best of 2025 Countdown Podcast , featuring guest critics Amy Taubin and Bilge Ebiri.

Also available in the links above: critic and programmer Inney Prakash’s list of the year’s Best Short Films , filmmaker and programmer Gina Telaroli’s list of the Best Restorations , critic and editor Gavin Smith’s list of the year’s Best Repertory Releases , and writing on the Best Scenes by Devika Girish ands the Best Performances by Michael Koresky.

Best Old-New Picks: every movie I saw as part of the “Through Cinema We Shall Rise!” retrospective at this year’s International Film Festival of Rotterdam, which marked the 70th anniversary of the historic Bandung Conference and the Afro-Asian Film Festivals it spawned. Special mentions: Turang (Bachtiar Siagan, 1958) and A Phu and His Wife (Vợ chồng A Phủ, 1960).

The order for me is not very important. I would just like to mention a few films with which I engaged in a deep, personal, and meaningful way this year. What strikes me about the list is that the works come from everywhere, including places where I’ve found it very difficult to find anything cinematically powerful lately: big-budget productions, blockbusters, films with a long list of labs in the opening credits, and works made by the usual suspects of the Cannes Film Festival. It’s exciting to notice that under all those logos, there’s still cinema breathing.

I don’t believe in the usual hierarchy between formats, so I wanted to name ten short and medium-length films that were as (or even more) important than the aforementioned features for me this year: Breu Febril (Wallace Douglas), Filme Sem Querer (Lincoln Péricles), Feiura Comovente (Ultra Martini), Piel de Toro Muerto (Aroldo Murguia), Abajo y a la Izquierda (Martín Baus), The Goblin Play (Chae Yu), Revolving Rounds (Johann Lurf, Christina Jauernik), Daimara y el Baile Zombie (Natalia Keiko, Tom Hamburguer), Bounded Intimacy (Ayanna Dozier).

A snapshot of my viewing up to 11/28/25. I haven’t had the chance to see a handful of “major titles” that likely would have impacted this list. These choices (and their ranking) are mine and mine alone; hence, they are flawed and imperfect, much like myself.
Come See Me In the Good Light

Throughout the entirety of 2025, I had the distinct honor and privilege of bearing witness to SO many phenomenal films from around the world, stewarded by brilliant filmmakers. These rankings are not to be taken LITERALLY but merely to operate as a humble offering to other curious moviegoers who want to know what 2025 was all about… rebellion, reconciliation, remixing, redistribution, and reimagining new worlds.
